Package dev.swordai.core.rl

package dev.swordai.core.rl
  • Class
    Description
    ActionSpace
    Seven independent categorical heads, one decision per game tick.
    ActorNet
    The acting network: two small CNNs over the enemy masks and an MLP over the vector input, joined into one trunk that feeds the action heads.
    AimMotor
    How a chosen camera speed becomes camera movement, modelled on a hand on a mouse.
    AimRule
    The camera is brought onto the opponent for the fighter in the ticks after it has been hit, for as long as it has not hit back: the ticks in which it is thrown into the air and comes down again, which is where the swing it owes is made (see AnswerRule), as a critical hit if the opponent is still in reach.
    AnswerRule
    A rule the fighter is held to, like the one about the sword's charge (SwingGate): hit, and not yet having hit back, it swings the moment its sword is back and the game has the opponent under its crosshair within reach.
    BackNudge
    The same kind of push as JumpNudge, for another choice in another situation: S, in the ticks right after a hit of a combo it is taking.
    ComboStrafe
    Out of the line of a combo, to the side: from the second hit in a row it is taking, A or D is held for ComboStrafe.TICKS ticks after each such hit, away from the way the opponent is moving across its view (or the other way from the last time, when it is not moving across).
    CriticNet
    Value network.
    DemoFile
    The user's own fights, step by step, for the network to learn from (/swordai demo; the user, 22 October: "I can do later but make it so I can start when I want").
    DemoFile.Fight
    One recorded fight, read back.
    DemoFile.Recorder
    A fight being recorded.
    DemoFile.Step
    One step as recorded.
    EdgeHold
    Spacing, the half of it that is about coming in: with the opponent just out of reach and its sword ready, the fighter does not walk into that reach.
    FallWatch
    What the fighter remembers of the last time a hit threw it into the air: whether the opponent was still within a sword's reach while it came down.
    FarRest
    A steady hand on an opponent that is far away.
    Fighter
    The trained policy as a player, with no learning attached: everything between what it senses on one tick and what it presses.
    HumanAction
    What a person playing did, as the action the network would have had to choose to do the same: for learning from the user's own fights (/swordai demo, DemoFile).
    JumpIn
    Three jumps that are made for the fighter, and what its keys do in the air of each.
    JumpNudge
    A push towards one choice in one situation, added to what the network itself says: jump, a few ticks after it has swung, standing on the ground with the opponent on screen.
    JumpReset
    The way out of a combo that gives the opponent no room: on the tick it learns of a hit of a combo it is taking (the second in a row or a later one), with its feet still on the ground, which they are for that one tick, it jumps with W and the sprint key held.
    Learner
    Ties the networks, the rollout buffer and PPO together.
    LostRule
    When the opponent has gone off the screen, the camera is not left to the network: it turns, at the hand's full speed, to the side the opponent was last seen on, and comes level (an opponent on the same ground is found at eye height), until the opponent is on screen again; then for a few ticks more it is brought onto the opponent, so that what is found is not lost again at once.
    MeetJump
    What it does about an opponent that is coming at it through the air: with its sword back and its feet on the ground, it runs in at that opponent while it is still going up, and swings the moment the game has it under the crosshair.
    MixIdea
    A plan the fighter is handed for its strafe keys, so that it fights with its feet as well: which side to go round the opponent on.
    Obs
    One observation: what the actor sees, plus the critic-only ground truth.
    ObsBuilder
    Packs the pieces of an observation into the layout declared in ObsSpec.
    ObsSpec
    Shapes of everything the networks consume.
    OpponentReader
    The opponent reader: what kind of opponent this is, read off the last three seconds of the fight.
    OpponentReader.Memory
    What it has been taught from: a sample of the labelled steps of the last updates, every OpponentReader.KEEP_EVERYth step, the oldest written over.
    OpponentReader.Stats
    What one round of learning did, for the log.
    OpponentReader.Window
    The window one fighter keeps of its fight, a sample every OpponentReader.STRIDE ticks, oldest first.
    Policy
    Maths for the factorised categorical policy: sampling, log-probabilities, entropy, gradients.
    Ppo
    Clipped-surrogate PPO with a separate critic.
    Ppo.SilStats
    What one self-imitation pass did; see Ppo.selfImitate(SilBuffer, Random, int, float, float, float).
    RewardScaler
    Divides rewards by a running estimate of the standard deviation of the discounted return, so the critic sees similar magnitudes in every curriculum stage.
    RhythmNet
    A memory of the last 3.2 seconds for the acting network (Config.rhythmNet): a causal temporal convolution (TCN: Bai, Kolter and Koltun 2018; WaveNet, van den Oord et al.
    Rollout
    Fixed-size on-policy buffer with generalised advantage estimation.
    SafeLearn
    Learning from fights against people without putting the trained network at risk.
    SafeLearn.Verdict
     
    SightTracker
    Turns the mask statistics of the newest frame into what the agent is told about the opponent's position, adding two things a player has without thinking about them: Knowing its own head movement. A frame is always a little old.
    SilBuffer
    Self-imitation learning (Oh et al., 2018): the steps that went far better than the critic expected, kept to be learned from again after the update that first saw them.
    StepBack
    After a hit of its own that has not sent the opponent away, it steps back out of that opponent's reach until its sword is nearly back, and only then comes in again.
    StraightIn
    With the opponent in view and out of reach, the strafe keys are let go of: it closes the distance running straight at the opponent.
    SwingGate
    No swing before the weapon is back.
    Tactic
    How it fights for the next half second: the choice the tactics model (TacticNet) makes, and what each choice turns on.
    Tactic.Clock
    When the next choice is due, for one fighter.
    TacticNet
    The tactics model: a small network of its own that chooses, every Tactic.EVERY ticks, how the fighter fights until the next choice (Tactic).
    TacticNet.Stats
    What one update of the tactics model did, for the log.
    UpdateStats
    Diagnostics from one PPO update.
